name: provenance
description: The record of one download, as written by bin/download.py: what was requested, the source URLs, assembly accession and taxon, the arguments that decided which variant of the assembly was delivered, checksums of the delivered files, a summary of the annotation, tool versions and the retrieval time in UTC. A passthrough - the file is stored as it was written. Tagged with the annotation release the download carried, or 'default' for a download of sequence alone, so a genome held at two annotation releases keeps a record of each. It lives in the vault, keyed by the genome's digest and reachable by every alias, so that it survives --cleanup and can be found by someone who did not build the vault: `refgenie seek <genome>/provenance`. Each record describes the download it came from. The vault's genome FASTA is kept from the first download of that sequence, so for a later release the record's 'genome' block describes a file with the same sequence, not necessarily the same bytes; the genome's digest is what identifies the sequence.
